content:
The following excerpt from Bhrgu's Yajñādhikāra
(Ch. 51) provides an insight into the Vaikhānasa outlook
with regard to its own Āgama-status. Even as the Veda
was later divided into four Books, so the Vaikhānasa-sūtra
became the four-fold śāstra

विष्णोस्तन्त्रं द्विधा प्रोक्तमर्चनार्थं तु वैदिकम्।
प्रथमं सौम्यमन्यत् तदाग्नेयं तान्त्रिकं भवेत् ॥
वैखानसेन सूत्रेण निषेकादि क्रियान्वितैः ।
ब्राह्मणैः क्रियामाणं यत्तत् सौम्यं वैदिकं मतम् ॥
विधिस्तु वेदमूलश्च दीक्षायुक्तश्च तान्त्रिकः ।
स चोक्तो द्विविधो मार्गः शुद्धमिश्रविभेदतः ।।
शुद्धं भागवतं प्रोक्तं पंचरात्रमथेतरत्।
सूतैर्वा सात्त्वतैर्वापि कृतं यच्छुद्धतान्त्रिकम्।।
तेषां शारीरसंस्कारास्तत्तत् तन्त्रेषु कीर्तिताः ।
न तेषां वेदमर्यादा सूतादीनां प्रवर्तते ।।
त्यक्ताऽत्मसूत्रविधिर्नानासूत्रार्थदर्शिभिः।
दीक्षितैः क्रियमाणं यत्तन्मिश्रमभिधीयते ।।
केवलं भुक्तिदं शुद्धं मिश्रं मुक्त्यैकसाधनम्।
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं सौम्यं इति पूर्वजदर्शनम् ॥
सौम्यं नारायणः प्राह वेदेभ्यः सारमुत्थितम्।
तस्माद् बह्मा विराट् तस्मात्स एव विखना मुनिः ॥

[Page 2]

ततोऽस्मदाद्या मुनयश्चत्वारो लेभिरे विधिम्।
तेभ्यः प्रादुरभूच्छास्त्रं उत्तमं चतुरात्मकम् ॥
वेदानां व्यसनादर्वाक् प्राग्रूपं मिलितं तु यत्।
तां तु वैखानसी शाखामिति प्रोक्तं विखनसा तथा ॥
तत्समष्ट्यात्मकं सूत्रं प्रोक्तं विखनसा तथा।
ऋगादिभेदसंभिन्ना व्यष्टिरूपेण सा पुनः।
ऋग्यजुः सामाथर्वेति चतुर्धा सा यथाऽभवत्।।
चतुर्धा व्यष्टिरूपेण तत्सूत्रं चाभवत्पुनः ।
आत्रेयं भार्गवं चैव मारीचं काश्यपं त्विति ॥

Then follows an enumeration of the works by the four
sages Atri, Bhrgu, Marici and Kāśyapa. There is also an
account of the content analysis of Bhrgu's works.
summary: This excerpt from Chapter 51 of Bhrgu's Yajñādhikāra presents the Vaikhānasa school's perspective on its own status. It classifies Viṣṇu's tantra into two main types: the Vedic (Saumya) and the Tantric (Āgneya). The Vaikhānasa path, based on the Vaikhānasasūtra and performed by Brahmins, is identified as the superior Saumya/Vedic tradition. The Tantric path is further subdivided into 'pure' (śuddha), identified with Pāñcarātra, and 'mixed' (miśra). The text traces the Vaikhānasa lineage from Nārāyaṇa to Vikhanas Muni. It then draws a parallel between the division of the primordial, unified Veda into four and the expansion of Vikhanas's singular sūtra into a four-fold śāstra by his four disciples: Atri, Bhrgu, Marīci, and Kāśyapa.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to provide a primary source text that explains the Vaikhānasa school's self-perception and its place within the broader Āgamic traditions. It aims to demonstrate how the Vaikhānasa tradition justifies its claim to a direct Vedic origin and superiority over other Tantric systems like Pāñcarātra, and how it conceptualizes the development of its own canonical literature.
key_information: The text is from Bhrgu's Yajñādhikāra, Chapter 51.
It provides the Vaikhānasa perspective on its own Āgama-status.
Viṣṇu's system (tantra) is categorized as twofold: Vedic (Saumya) and Tantric (Āgneya).
The Vaikhānasa tradition is equated with the Saumya (Vedic) path.
The Tantric path is divided into śuddha (pure, e.g., Pāñcarātra) and miśra (mixed).
The Vaikhānasa lineage is traced from Nārāyaṇa -> Brahmā -> Virāṭ -> Vikhanas Muni.
An analogy is made: the single Veda becoming four is like the single Vaikhānasasūtra becoming the four-fold śāstra.
The four-fold śāstra was developed by the sages Atri, Bhrgu, Marīci, and Kāśyapa.

tables_and_data.description: Classification of Āgamic Traditions according to the Vaikhānasa view presented in the text.
tables_and_data.data_summary:
The text presents a three-tiered classification:
1.  **Saumya (Vedic):** The Vaikhānasa tradition itself, yielding both worldly enjoyment (bhukti) and liberation (mukti).
2.  **Śuddha Tāntrika (Pure Tantric):** The Pāñcarātra and Bhāgavata traditions, yielding only worldly enjoyment (bhukti).
3.  **Miśra (Mixed Tantric):** Practices by those who have abandoned their own sūtra traditions, yielding only liberation (mukti).
